A1.justification: The PDFs clearly describe successive versions of the same work, with C-BBL developed into UGS, and all supplied pages are readable. Neither contains an appendix. However, v2 Section 3.1 refers to supplementary derivations absent from the supplied material, limiting assessment of those derivations.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations on VisDrone, VOC, and COCO, component and parameter ablations, and gradient and convergence analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original UGS evaluations on four benchmarks, component and parameter ablations, qualitative examples, training-cost measurements, and gradient-variance analysis.

M1.justification: UGS retains C-BBL's quantized classification-based localization but changes uncertainty minimization from |H(p*) - H(p)| to H(p). It also adds uncertainty-guided refinement through adversarial perturbations of FPN features and an additional refinement objective (v2 Sections 3.2.2–3.2.3). These substantially change training beyond renaming.

E1.justification: v2 adds SODA-A alongside retained VisDrone, VOC, and COCO evaluations. SODA-A introduces oriented-box aerial detection with rotated detectors, substantially extending the task coverage beyond the horizontal-box evaluations in v1.

E2.justification: The VisDrone comparisons add FCOS, DINO-5scale, QueryDet, DetectoRS, CZDet, DQ-DETR, and CEASC, while removing ATSS, plain RetinaNet, and standalone YOLOv4/v5 rows. GFocal/GFL is matched across naming. v2 Table 6 additionally compares IoU loss, gradient clipping, and Bayesian YOLO.

E3.justification: v2 introduces DINO's 24-epoch AdamW training, DETR-style augmentation, and 1,500-prediction test limit, plus SODA-specific evaluation and resource-profiling procedures. Figure 2 changes its reported sample count from 50 to 100 and early epoch from 0 to 1; this does not establish a rerun. v1's VisDrone test-dev evaluation, including 2016-pixel inputs, is omitted.

E4.justification: v2 adds UR and loss-weight ablations, broader range/modulator sensitivity studies, gradient-variance and computational-cost analyses, and uncertainty/occlusion examples. The grid-number study is retained and expanded. v1's top-two versus full-band restoration ablation (Table 3) and TPH-YOLOv5 convergence curves (Figure 6) are removed.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.6 newly specifies estimating gradient variance across 100 training iterations and reporting mean variance ratios by anchor size. This adds within-training variability estimation, without establishing additional independent runs. Neither version reports training seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for detection scores.

E6.justification: C-BBL's TPH-YOLOv5 AP values of 27.1/40.1 at 640/1536 resolution are replaced by UGS values of 29.0/41.7 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 2). General-detection and ablation results change, new DINO/SODA/diagnostic results appear, and test-dev results disappear. v2 Table 1 implies Faster R-CNN and GFL gains of 2.9 and 2.8 AP, conflicting with Section 4.2's 2.6 and 3.5.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's first-order regression analysis with Hessian/Lipschitz arguments (Equations 3–7), revises target and entropy formulas, and adds adversarial min-max and perturbation formulations (Equations 14–15). Some new mathematics is inconsistent: Equation 13 gives a probability derivative as a logit derivative. Referenced supplementary derivations are unavailable.

C1.justification: The principal contribution expands from confidence-driven localization with entropy matching to gradient stabilization through curvature analysis and a dual uncertainty mechanism including adversarial refinement. The abstract now explicitly claims compatibility with anchor-free and transformer detectors and highlights DINO-5scale's 2.6 AP gain, extending v1's contribution framing.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive explanations connecting small-object convergence to loss curvature, non-uniform grids to label imbalance, and adversarial refinement to occlusion/noise robustness. It interprets UM as reducing prediction and gradient variance and discusses computational overhead, replacing v1's emphasis on target-entropy lower-bound matching and restoration stability.

D1.justification: v2 adds MMDetection implementation information, UR hyperparameters, DINO settings, and resource measurements, and reports RTX 3090 rather than 3090Ti hardware. Conversely, v1's exact VOC/COCO splits, VOC input-resolution/batch settings, and YOLO quantization parameters disappear. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to all retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 replaces much of the generic detection review with a dedicated uncertainty-estimation discussion and expands recent small-object detection coverage. It explicitly builds on GFL V1 and offset-bin classification, and introduces adversarial-feature learning and sharpness-aware optimization connections, materially revising the method's relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Quantization and classification explanations are consolidated, separate preliminaries are absorbed into gradient analysis, and ablations move after the main evaluations. The title, method terminology, authorship/affiliations, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The Faster R-CNN pipeline in v1 Figure 3 becomes an FCOS/FPN diagram with adversarial refinement in v2 Figure 4. Gradient visualizations are redesigned; uncertainty and variance plots replace the old IoU and convergence plots. Comparison tables are reorganized, with separate YOLO, SODA, and cost displays and substantially revised ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through broader evaluations, UR ablations, gradient diagnostics, and cost measurements. However, its new entropy-gradient formula (Equation 13) is incorrect for softmax logits and contradicts the bounded-gradient claim. Several claimed gains conflict with Table 1, and useful implementation details are removed. These benefits and problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
